contents.name: §6.5 General parabolic equations ($v_t+Lv=f$, weak maximum principles, strong maximum principle for general $L$)
contents.reason: General second-order parabolic operators with drift and potential are treated on the later analytic-semigroup and Schauder/Lp pages, not on this page, whose operator is exactly $\partial_t-\Delta$.

contents.name: PDE-8 authoritative §12.4 addition: Supremum norm stability for forced heat problems
contents.proof_mapping: Fix t; compactness and continuity make m continuous. For w=u-v and M=max(a,b_t), the barriers M+integral_0^s m and -M-integral_0^s m bound w on the parabolic boundary and have respectively larger and smaller forcing. Apply the comparison corollary on the truncated cylinder. The bounds hold at every s<=t, and integration monotonicity gives the stated supremum bound. No whole-space uniqueness or future Sobolev estimate is used.

contents.name: PDE-8 authoritative §12.4 addition: Strict positivity propagates to later interior times
contents.proof_mapping: If u(x,t)=0 at a time later than s_*, then -u is a subsolution with global maximum 0 at that interior point on the cylinder truncated at t. Strong maximum makes u=0 throughout the connected backward cylinder, contradicting u(x_*,s_*)>0. For positive initial trace, continuity supplies a positive point at a time s_* between 0 and each prescribed t.

contents.name: PDE-8 authoritative §12.4 addition: Energy identity for the forced Dirichlet heat equation
contents.proof_mapping: Differentiate the energy integral using continuity of u and u_t on the compact cylinder. Substitute u_t=Delta u+f. First Green identity with v=u gives integral u Delta u=-integral |Du|^2 because the trace u vanishes. Rearrange; integrate the continuous equality for the balance. Carry exactly the Green supplier choice assumption.

contents.name: PDE-8 authoritative §12.4 addition: L1 in time estimate for Lp Duhamel forcing
contents.proof_mapping: For finite p strong continuity of H makes the orbit of each step-function value strongly measurable; approximate f pointwise by simple functions and use contraction to pass to the limit. For p=infinity, the L1-continuous kernel map tau->Gamma_tau on every compact subset of (0,infinity) makes tau->H_tau g norm continuous there for every fixed g; exhaust s<t by countably many closed intervals. The value at the singleton s=t is harmless. Thus each simple approximation produces a strongly measurable integrand for all p. Contraction bounds its norm by ||f(s)||p. Bochner integrability and its norm inequality give the claim.

contents.name: PDE-8 authoritative §12.4 addition: Spatial smoothing of forcing separated from the observation time
contents.proof_mapping: Kernel derivative estimates apply uniformly because t-s>=epsilon. The Lp-to-Linfinity bound for each derivative supplies an integrable time majorant proportional to ||f(s)||p and yields an everywhere-defined smooth representative by differentiation under the scalar integral; the same bound for the next derivative proves continuity. Integrate the Lp-to-Lq derivative estimate and apply the Bochner norm inequality. No integration of a singular near-diagonal derivative estimate occurs.

contents.name: PDE-8 authoritative §12.4 addition: Incompatible initial and boundary values prevent corner continuity
contents.proof_mapping: Continuity at (0,0) along the initial edge forces u(0,0)=lim_(x->0+)1=1, while continuity along the lateral edge forces u(0,0)=lim_(t->0+)0=0. The contradictory limits refute the existence assertion. No sine-series convergence or corner differentiability claim is used.

§6.1 Maximum principle discussion: at an interior or final-time maximum $u_t\ge0$ and $\Delta u\le0$, so $u_t-\Delta u\ge0$; $f\le0$ forces the maximum onto the lateral boundary or $t=0$, and $f\le0$ in general follows by a perturbation argument

contents.name: PDE-8 authoritative §12.4 addition: Compactly supported nonzero terminal profiles are outside the heat range
contents.proof_mapping: By the published PDE-7 analyticity theorem the representative is real analytic. Fix x and a coordinate direction e_1. Its restriction s->u(x+s e_1) is analytic on R: substitute this affine line in the supplied Taylor expansion. Compact support gives zero on a half-line. Apply the real analytic interval identity theorem to real and imaginary parts; evaluating at s=0 gives u(x)=0. Since x was arbitrary, u=0. No claim about injectivity or unbounded-data solutions is needed.

contents.name: PDE-8 authoritative §12.4 addition: Finite sine sums admit a backward Dirichlet heat solution
contents.proof_mapping: Each finite summand has time derivative -k^2 times itself and second spatial derivative -k^2 times itself. Finite summation preserves the PDE, smoothness and both zero boundary values. At t=T all exponential factors are 1. The assertion is existence for each finite datum, with no uniform inverse bound and no assertion for arbitrary infinite series.
